title: Floods and the Duplication of Production: Evidence from the Global Car Industry
abstract: arXiv:2611.01329v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Floods are becoming more frequent and can disrupt global supply chains. We study how multinational car makers adapt vehicle and key parts production to flood risk, and how their choices interact with insurance and public flood defences. Using plant-level data and a manually verified flood record in a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that car makers duplicate production rather than move it away from flooded plants. Even more than five years after a flood, an engine is 19 percentage points more likely to be made in two or more plants, usually abroad and for cars assembled nearby, while the flooded plant's output shows no persistent decline beyond a temporary loss in the flood year. Firms duplicate only where adjustment costs are low, i.e. when a plant of theirs abroad already makes the same engine family. Flooded vehicle model versions are duplicated only temporarily, and transmission programs are not duplicated. Suggest

translated_title: 洪水与生产的重复布局：来自全球汽车产业的证据
translated_abstract: 洪水正变得日益频繁，并可能扰乱全球供应链。我们研究了跨国汽车制造商如何调整整车及关键零部件的生产以应对洪水风险，以及这些选择如何与保险和公共防洪设施相互作用。利用工厂层面数据和人工核验的洪水记录，采用交错双重差分设计，我们发现汽车制造商选择复制生产，而非将生产迁离受灾工厂。即使在洪水发生五年多之后，一台发动机由两个或更多工厂（通常位于国外，并为附近组装的汽车配套）生产的可能性高出19个百分点，而受灾工厂的产出除洪水当年出现暂时性损失外，并未表现出持续下降。企业只在调整成本较低时才复制生产，即当其海外工厂已经生产同一系列发动机时。受灾车型的整车版本只是暂时被复制，而变速器项目则不会被复制。
tldr: 该研究发现，面对洪水风险，跨国汽车制造商倾向于在海外复制关键零部件（如发动机）的生产以增强供应链韧性，而非将生产迁离受灾工厂，且只有在调整成本较低时才会采取这种复制策略。
en_tdlr: Facing flood risk, multinational car makers build supply chain resilience by duplicating key parts production (e.g., engines) abroad rather than relocating away from flooded plants, and only do so when adjustment costs are low.
